description_full: Central Pattana Public Company Limited develops and manages real estate properties in Thailand. It constructs, develops, and manages shopping malls, office buildings, hotels, and residential projects for lease. The company also provides utility services in shopping centers, property management consulting, corporate, and food center services. In addition, it engages in the operation of play lands and water theme parks in shopping centers; investment in real estate; education services; sale of land, houses, and condominium units; and management of a real estate investment trust. Central Pattana Public Company Limited was founded in 1980 and is headquartered in Bangkok, Thailand.
ceo_bio: Mr. Chanavat  Uahwatanasakul | President, CEO & Director | Age 52
financial_summary: CENTRAL PATTANA PUBLIC CO is a mid-cap real estate business with a $7.0B market cap on $1.5B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +14% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +3.3pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 7% against a 7% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically. Gross margins of 54% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $1.1B in free cash flow — roughly 74 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.02× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 3.7× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage runs at 5.5×.

Shareholder yield of 4.1% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 2.0× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

It runs a 54% gross margin and converts 74% of revenue into free cash flow.

Warning signs: an Altman Z of 1.58 in the distress zone, which caps the rating at HOLD.

growth: Revenue has compounded at 14.4% over 3 years.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
